Kutaisi-Georgia.name: Kutaisi

Shusha-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Exact 1886 family lists (26,806), 1897 Russian Imperial Census (25,881), and 1917 Kavkazskiy Kalendar (43,869), anchored to Karabakh Khanate capital (~12,000 in 1830) and cultural/trade prosperity (Swietochowski).

Akhaltsikhe-Georgia.name: Akhaltsikhe
Akhaltsikhe-Georgia.evidence_basis: Exact 1886 family lists (16,116) and 1897 Russian Imperial Census (15,357), capturing 1828 conquest transition from Ottoman pashalik to Russian uyezd centre and 1915 Kavkazskiy Kalendar tally.

Telavi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Exact 1886 family lists (11,214) and 1897 Russian Imperial Census (13,929) for Kakheti's administrative seat, scaled to early-19th-century Kakhetian town records and 1915 Kavkazskiy Kalendar (Jaoshvili).

Gori-Georgia.name: Gori

Lankaran-Azerbaijan.name: Lankaran
Lankaran-Azerbaijan.evidence_basis: Exact 1897 Russian Imperial Census (8,733) as Lenkoran uyezd centre and Caspian port in Baku Governorate, anchored to post-1813 Talysh Khanate annexation and 1915 Kavkazskiy Kalendar.

Borjomi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Founded 1829 as a Russian mineral-spring spa and later Grand Ducal estate; permanent settlement assessed from Gori uyezd records, 1894 railway/bottling expansion, and Kavkazskiy Kalendar (Jaoshvili).

Tkibuli-Georgia.evidence_basis: Assessed from Kutaisi uyezd colliery workforce records after 1846 coal mining inception and 1887 Kutaisi-Tkibuli railway opening, cross-checked against Kavkazskiy Kalendar (Jaoshvili).

Lagodekhi-Georgia.evidence_basis: Established 1830 as a Russian Caucasian Line garrison post against Lezgin raids; growth as a Sighnaghi uyezd garrison and tobacco-farming town assessed from 1886 family lists and Kavkazskiy Kalendar.

Khachmaz-Azerbaijan.name: Khachmaz
